title: Decoupled Diffusion Sparks Adaptive Scene Generation

control_signal.value: Goal points (future target states, e.g. lane-centre points) for selected agents such as the ego and an attack vehicle; no goal means free exploration.

control_mechanism.value: Noise-masking training with per-token noise levels; at inference goal tokens are set to zero noise (low-noise goals) while other tokens stay high-noise, steering generation without adaptation. Classifier guidance adds realism rubrics.

base_model.value: Decoupled diffusion transformer built on SimpleDiffusion with four temporal and spatial blocks (AdaLN), Perceiver IO map encoder; vectorized scene tokens with independent noise states.

datasets.value: Trained on nuPlan, Waymo and self-collected Nexus-Data (540 hours of simulated safety-critical scenarios from a simulator with adversarial interactions); nuPlan closed-loop Val14 evaluation.

metrics.value: ADE, off-road rate, collision rate, trajectory instability Mk, composite realism metric, Waymo sim-agent evaluation, nuPlan closed-loop Score, collision score, progress score.

controllability_evidence.value: Goal-conditioned generation on nuPlan: ADE 1.28 for Nexus and 1.12 for Nexus-Full, versus 1.93 for GUMP. Abstract reports a 40% reduction in displacement error.

stated_limitations.value: No visual generation, limiting sensor-data uses. Failure cases show incorrect collisions and difficulty in complex road networks due to limited map information.

notes: Control is goal-state conditioning via noise levels, not a separate conditioning branch. Classifier guidance is used only for human-behaviour realism rubrics (collision avoidance, comfort, on-road).
